title: Family Theme Parks: Tickets, Offers & Money-Saving Tips
description: Compare family theme parks in the UK, US and Europe, from LEGOLAND and Alton Towers to Disney, Universal and Efteling, with real ways to save on tickets.
h1: Family theme parks: where to go and how to pay less
intro: Coasters for thrill-seekers, gentle rides for toddlers and castles for everyone. Here are the best family theme parks near and far, with honest tips from Scout on who each one suits.

image.alt: A roller coaster at an amusement park

blocks.title: Scout’s theme park rule of thumb
blocks.text: Pick the park for your youngest child, then find the extras for the oldest. A toddler at a thrill park is a long day for everyone.
facts: Annual pass if you go 2+ times

blocks.title: Family theme parks we love
blocks.intro: Filter by where you want to go. Every card has ways to save and a tip from Scout.

items.title: Alton Towers Resort

image.alt: Riders with arms in the air on a roller coaster

items.text: The UK’s best-known thrill park, with big roller coasters for teens and CBeebies Land for little ones, plus a water park and hotels on site.
saves: Included in Merlin Annual Passes (check exclusion dates)
A Tesco Clubcard Reward Partner in 2026: check the Clubcard app for current exchanges
Book online before you go: gate prices are usually the highest
items.scout: Split the day: thrill rides first while queues are short, CBeebies Land after lunch when little legs need a slower pace.

items.title: LEGOLAND Windsor Resort

image.alt: Yellow, red, blue and green toy building bricks

items.text: Built for families with children aged roughly 2 to 12: gentle coasters, driving schools, MINILAND models and plenty of hands-on play.
saves: Included in Merlin Annual Passes
Listed on the National Rail Days Out Guide with a rail-ticket discount in 2026
Weekdays outside school holidays are usually the quietest and cheapest
items.scout: Under-3s go free, so it’s great value while they’re tiny. Check ride height limits before you promise anything!

items.title: Chessington World of Adventures

image.alt: People riding a spinning fairground ride

items.text: A rare mix of family rides and a zoo in one ticket, which makes it a strong all-rounder for mixed-age families.
saves: Included in Merlin Annual Passes
Animal areas are a calm break when queues build up
items.scout: Two days out for the price of one: plan your route around the animal talks and feeding times.

items.title: Paultons Park, home of Peppa Pig World

image.alt: A happy family running together in a sunlit garden

items.text: Peppa Pig World is a toddler favourite, and the park’s new Viking-themed land, Valgard, opened in spring 2026 with bigger rides for older kids.
saves: Not part of the Merlin pass: check Paultons’ own annual passes if you live nearby
Closed in January and on some winter dates, so check the calendar first
items.scout: Peppa Pig World is busiest first thing. Head there in the afternoon and do the rest of the park in the morning.

items.title: Thorpe Park Resort

image.alt: A roller coaster track against a blue sky

items.text: Big, fast rides aimed at teens and adults, and a short hop from London. Younger children will find fewer rides that fit them.
saves: Included in Merlin Annual Passes
Online, date-based tickets are usually cheaper than buying on the day
items.scout: Best for teens and thrill-seeking grown-ups. With under-8s, LEGOLAND or Chessington is the better pick.

items.title: Blackpool Pleasure Beach

image.alt: A roller coaster at an amusement park

items.text: A classic seaside park with historic wooden coasters and a younger kids’ area, right by the beach and the famous promenade.
saves: Kids Pass has listed discounts here in 2026: check the app before booking
Pair it with free beach time and the promenade to stretch the day
items.scout: Blackpool’s Merlin attractions (the Tower, SEA LIFE and more) are no longer included on new or renewed Merlin passes, so price them separately.

items.title: Walt Disney World Resort

image.alt: Cinderella Castle at Magic Kingdom, Walt Disney World, Orlando

items.text: Four theme parks (Magic Kingdom, EPCOT, Hollywood Studios and Animal Kingdom) plus two water parks. It’s a holiday, not a day out, so plan several days.
saves: Children under 3 don’t need a park ticket
Multi-day tickets cost less per day than single days
Check Disney’s official special offers page before booking
items.scout: Don’t try to do it all. Two parks done well beat four done in a rush, especially with little ones.

items.title: Universal Orlando Resort

image.alt: A castle-style building lit up at night

items.text: Universal Studios Florida, Islands of Adventure and Epic Universe (opened 2025), plus Volcano Bay water park. The Wizarding World of Harry Potter is spread across all three theme parks.
saves: Multi-day tickets are better value per day
For 2026, 3-day-plus tickets include Epic Universe visits; 2-day tickets don’t, so check before you buy
You need a park-to-park ticket to ride the Hogwarts Express between the two original parks
items.scout: Harry Potter fans: Diagon Alley and Hogsmeade are in different parks. Get a park-to-park ticket or you’ll miss half the magic.

items.title: Disneyland Resort

image.alt: A fairy-tale castle lit up at night

items.text: The original Disneyland Park and Disney California Adventure sit side by side, so it’s easier to tackle in two or three days than Florida.
saves: Under-3s go free
Multi-day tickets lower the cost per day
Southern California residents sometimes get special ticket offers: check Disney’s offers page
items.scout: The two parks are a short walk apart, so a park hopper ticket is easy to use here.

items.title: Disneyland Paris

image.alt: Sleeping Beauty Castle at Disneyland Paris

items.text: Disneyland Park plus Disney Adventure World (the renamed Walt Disney Studios Park), where World of Frozen opened on 29 March 2026.
saves: Children under 3 go free
Check the official offers page: Disneyland Paris often runs seasonal hotel and ticket offers
UK tour operators sometimes include free child places on packages
items.scout: Go for at least two days so you can do both parks without rushing. Frozen fans should head to World of Frozen early.

items.title: Efteling

image.alt: Fireworks over a fairy-tale castle at night

items.text: One of Europe’s most-loved parks, famous for its enchanted Fairytale Forest, plus coasters for older kids and grown-ups.
saves: Date-based online tickets: quieter days cost less
Holiday parks nearby can work out cheaper than on-site hotels for longer stays
items.scout: The Fairytale Forest is a walk, not a ride, so it works brilliantly for toddlers and grandparents alike.

items.title: Europa-Park

image.alt: A roller coaster at an amusement park

items.text: Germany’s largest theme park, themed by European countries, with the Rulantica indoor water park next door.
saves: Multi-day stays make more sense than a single day here
Combine with Rulantica on a separate day rather than squeezing both into one
items.scout: It’s big! Two days lets you enjoy it without sprinting between countries.

items.title: PortAventura World

image.alt: Water slides at a water park

items.text: A beach-holiday-friendly resort with PortAventura Park, Ferrari Land and Caribe Aquatic Park, near the Costa Dorada beaches.
saves: Hotel stays often include park access: compare packages with separate tickets
Combine with a beach holiday rather than a standalone trip
items.scout: Perfect for a sun-and-rides holiday. Pack the suncream and plan indoor breaks in the hottest hours.

items.title: LEGOLAND Billund

image.alt: A close-up of colourful toy building bricks

items.text: The original LEGOLAND, opened in 1968, a short walk from LEGO House, the brick-lover’s experience centre.
saves: Combine LEGOLAND and LEGO House in one trip to make the travel worthwhile
Check seasonal opening: the park isn’t open all year
items.scout: A dream trip for LEGO fans. Book LEGO House separately: it’s its own attraction with its own tickets.

items.title: Parc Astérix

image.alt: People riding a spinning fairground ride

items.text: A big, funny, very French park themed on the Astérix comics, with strong coasters and family rides.
saves: Online, date-based tickets are usually cheaper than the gate
Easy to combine with a Paris city break
items.scout: A great second park if you’re already doing Disneyland Paris, and a different flavour of fun.

items.title: Tivoli Gardens

image.alt: A fairy-tale castle lit up at night

items.text: One of the world’s oldest amusement parks (opened 1843), in the heart of Copenhagen, with gardens, rides and festive seasonal lights.
saves: Entry and rides are priced separately: an unlimited-ride wristband suits ride-hungry kids, single entry suits strollers
Combine with a city break
items.scout: Visit after dark: the lights are the real star. Halloween and Christmas seasons are magical.

sections.h2: How to save on theme park tickets
sections.html:
• Book online, in advance. Most parks use date-based pricing, and buying on the gate is usually the most expensive way in.
  • Go off-peak. Term-time weekdays are often cheaper and quieter than weekends and school holidays.
  • Check who goes free. Under-3s are free at most big parks, including Disney and LEGOLAND.
  • Use the train. The National Rail Days Out Guide lists rail-ticket discounts at some parks.
  • Think annual pass. If you’ll visit two or more Merlin parks in a year, compare the Merlin Annual Pass.
  • Use rewards. Tesco Clubcard vouchers and Kids Pass can cut the cost at some parks.

sections.h2: Making the most of the day
sections.html: Arrive before opening, head to the most popular ride first, and save shows and gentle rides for the busy middle of the day. Ask about rider switch (also called baby swap) so grown-ups can take turns without queuing twice. Our theme park queue tips go into more detail.

faqs.q: What is the best UK theme park for young children?
faqs.a: LEGOLAND Windsor and Paultons Park (home of Peppa Pig World) are designed with young children in mind. Chessington mixes gentle rides with a zoo, which suits mixed-age families.

faqs.q: Are under-3s free at theme parks?
faqs.a: At most big parks, yes, including Walt Disney World, Disneyland Paris and LEGOLAND. Always check the park’s own ticket page, because age rules vary.

faqs.q: Is it cheaper to buy theme park tickets on the day?
faqs.a: Usually not. Most parks charge the highest prices at the gate and reward booking online in advance, especially for quieter dates.
